newsitem.title: UK: National grid says lodges pensions appeal.
newsitem.headline: National grid says lodges pensions appeal.

text.p: Britain's electricity transmission group National Grid Company Plc said on Wednesday it had lodged appeals to the High Court against a ruling on February 7 it must pay 46.3 million stg to its pension scheme.
The decision, made by the Pensions Ombudsman, would have meant an increase of 600,000 pounds a year in the company's contributions.
National Grid said it had also applied for a stay of the directions, pending the appeal.

"National Grid believes that the arrangements it made to deal with the 1992 surplus were properly and lawfully made...and that the arrangements represented a fair allocation," the company said in a statement.
The Pensions Ombudsman's ruling concerned payments to the pension fund which were not paid while the scheme was in surplus, plus interest.
The Ombudsman also ruled that National Grid should make proper arrangements to deal with the surplus.
